section.title: Introduction
section.p: The ImageFileConvert module provides an interface for converting between different image formats through a simple defined interface. Whilst this interface may not be perfectly suited to all image formats, it can be extended through flagged operations to provide greater flexibility and to allow more functional conversions to be made.
Because ImageFileConvert and ImageFileRender complement one another it is recommended that users of either familiarise themselves with the other.

subsection.title: Flags common to output type 'Sprite'
subsection.p: Because Sprite is a common type to convert to a number of flags are defined as being used for all conversions.

bitfield-table.bit: Create a sprite, rather than a sprite file (this option is provided by the ImageFileConvert module)

subsection.title: Flags common to output type 'JPEG'
subsection.p: Because JPEG is a common type to convert to a number of flags are defined as being used for all conversions.

bitfield-table.bit: Output JPEG will be monochrome (otherwise it will be colour)

subsection.p: The duplication of 75% in both 0 and 6 is to allow users to leave the flags unset and get a sensible default conversion quality.

subsection.title: Flags common to input type 'Sprite'
subsection.p: Although sprite is a common filetype to convert from none of the flags are reserved for all conversions.

subsection.title: Operations common to the output type 'Sprite'
subsection.p: The following operation is provided by for conversions to the output type 'Sprite'.

offset-table.offset: Bits per pixel in the image

subsection.p: The image flags in R3 are:

bitfield-table.bit: Image is colour (otherwise image is greyscale)
Image has alpha channel or mask

Interlace type:
No interlacing Adam7 interlacing Vertical interlacing Reserved

subsection.p: This operation reads information about the image which is common to most bitmap-type operations.
